descriptionChirho: The Aramaic noun corresponding to Biblical Hebrew erets, denoting the earth or land as a physical and political entity. Predominantly found in Daniel (chapters 2, 4, 6, 7) and Ezra 5:11, with one occurrence in Jeremiah 10:11. Used for the earth as the physical world in contrast to heaven (Dan 6:27 'in the heavens and on the earth'), for the whole earth as a domain of royal authority (Dan 2:35, 39; 4:1, 10-11, 15, 20, 22, 35), and for particular lands or territories (Dan 7:4, 17, 23). The occurrence glossed 'lower' in Daniel 2:39 describes a kingdom 'inferior' (literally 'earthward/lower') to Nebuchadnezzar's, using the same noun in a contextual extension meaning 'lower in status,' not a distinct lexical sense. Prepositional variants (in the earth, from the earth, and earth) are syntactic, not semantic differences.
